referenceSource: Synthetic French speech generated with mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-VoiceDesign-8bit during the operator's voice comparison. Not a human recording.
referenceText: Bonjour, prenez le temps de vous installer. Aujourd’hui, nous allons découvrir ensemble une histoire simple et agréable. Écoutez tranquillement, puis répétez à votre rythme.
selection: Operator preferred this conditioned Chatterbox voice to Qwen and Kokoro in the comparison.
processing: Speak each entry inside a French carrier phrase, compare the local Whisper transcript with the target text or its French phonemes, then extract the vocabulary item. New renders use DTW anchors and a quiet transition; each cached recording records its own alignment method.
validatorDependencies: whisper-cli with the local large-v3-turbo model and DTW token alignment, espeak-ng and ffmpeg.
pronunciationCaveat: Synthetic speech can mispronounce or add words; audio checks are not native-speaker certification.

build.description: 8-bit MLX conversion (affine, group size 64) of the official checkpoint, made with mlx-audio 0.5.1. The official config.json says model_type higgs_multimodal_qwen3, which mlx-audio does not recognise, so the conversion reads a copy of the snapshot whose config.json says higgs_audio_v3. The converter drops the audio codec, so codec.safetensors is the codec tensors from the same checkpoint in float16 (byte-identical to the codec.safetensors of whitelabel/mlx-q6-higgs-tts-3-4b), and model.safetensors.index.json is removed so mlx-audio finds that file.
build.selection: On the 20 hardest words of the precision check, three seeds, both candidate references, it was misheard 2 times in 120 against 7 for the 6-bit community quant whitelabel/mlx-q6-higgs-tts-3-4b. It costs about 6 GB of memory and 1.2 s a word.

swedish.referenceSource: LibriVox recording of Valda berättelser by Selma Lagerlöf, chapter 2, read in Swedish by Anna Sofia Andersson: 0:58.15 to 1:10.05 of valdaberattelser_02_lagerlof_128kb.mp3 (https://archive.org/details/valda_berattelser_2304_librivox), mono 24 kHz. A native woman's careful read-aloud voice; median pitch 205 Hz.
swedish.referenceAttribution: Read by Anna Sofia Andersson for LibriVox.
swedish.referenceText: Den spelmannen som fanns i Svartsjö ville han nämligen inte kalla. Han hette Jan Öster och nämndemannen visste nog att han hade ett ganska stort rykte.
swedish.selection: Chosen over Karin Nilsson (K-podd, Riksantikvarieämbetet, CC BY 2.5 SE) in a 166-clip precision check: 4 failures against 11, a calmer pace (3.6 against 5.2 syllables a second in sentences) and no cloned room tone.
swedish.processing: Say the word alone, capitalised, with a full stop and a pause tag, then cut the clip 250 ms after the measured end of speech. KB-Whisper must hear the cut clip as the word (or a spelling espeak-ng pronounces the same), and nothing in it may rise above the take's own floor after the word, with its last 150 ms quiet. A failing word is re-rendered with the next seed; after three it is written anyway, flagged in the manifest and listed in failures.json.
swedish.validatorDependencies: whisper-cli with KBLab/kb-whisper-large ggml-model.bin at revision d5d5984b4d8f7c4847a8ea203f1976285fb28300 from the Hugging Face cache, espeak-ng (sv) and ffmpeg.
swedish.pronunciationCaveat: Synthetic speech can mispronounce; vowel length (tak against tack) is the slip Whisper catches least reliably, since it leans toward the commoner word for a word said alone.
